details.label: Discussion
details.text: A loosely organized cold-pool-driven MCS, with a history of numerous damaging gusts, is cresting the Blue Ridge Mountains and is poised to approach the Chesapeake Bay over the next few hours. Surface temperatures remain in the 80s F, with low-level lapse rates still around 7 C/km per 22Z mesoanalysis. Nonetheless, nocturnal cooling will begin soon along the East Coast, which will further reduce instability. In the near-term a few damaging gusts remain possible with storms along the leading edge of a cold pool. The best chance for a damaging or even severe gust will be with storms propagating toward central VA, where boundary-layer instability is strongest

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Multicell storms continue to propagate southeastward amid 2000-3000 J/kg MLCAPE, supported mainly by 7-7.5 C/km boundary-layer lapse rates and 70s F surface dewpoints. These favorable thermodynamic conditions are prevalent along and south of an outflow boundary left behind by earlier thunderstorms. Storms traversing this boundary will have the best chance for producing a damaging or severe gust, and a brief tornado cannot be completely ruled out

details.text: Large hail and damaging wind threat continues within WW587

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A cluster of storms south of the Denver Metro has produced severe gusts up to 62 mph. Mode remains fairly mixed, with multi-cell clusters and supercells ongoing across portions of eastern Colorado. The environment remains moderately unstable with around 30-35 kts of deep layer shear. Severe potential will likely increase with movement eastward into more available 60 F degree dew points. Supercells with large hail potential will continue over the next couple of hours before eventual transition to one or more linear clusters. An increase in the damaging wind threat is expected eastward into the lower Plains by the evening
